finding: Private bearer links enter application telemetry. Help events explicitly send the raw `page_path`; error reporting sends the raw `route`. GA redaction misses mixed-case URLs that the router accepts and omits sensitive custom-event/referrer overrides. A disclosed adoption token authorizes applicant name, email/phone and visit preferences.
status_and_next_action: **Fixed; verified locally.** Shared case-insensitive redaction now covers Help/error route fields and application-generated GA page/referrer fields. Eleven regression tests and three built-browser status-page cases pass. Requires the relevant collector to be configured; production transmission remains unverified.

finding: Staff permissions differ between the API and database. The CRM API permits treasurer/admin, while RLS permits staff to read/update supporter and consent rows directly. Existing column grants preserve supporter mutations, bypassing the API's role and optimistic-version workflow.
status_and_next_action: **Open; code-only; product/security decision.** Decide intended staff CRM powers, then align API, RLS and column grants. Direct mutations are audited by later triggers; this is not a claim of missing audit logs. Deployed grants were not inspected.

finding: The isolated acceptance runner can report success while skipping intended DB coverage. It selects 90 DB/integration files, but 29 reference opt-in variables absent from its environment setup. Some suites reject its dedicated port, so merely enabling flags is insufficient. Its spawned command also omits the normal `--isolate` test mode.
status_and_next_action: **Open; verified.** Two representative suites yielded 0 pass, 69 skip, 0 fail, exit 0 with their missing opt-ins. Introduce an explicit supported-suite manifest, compatible disposable targets, isolation and a coverage/skip failure policy.

finding: CI treats the RLS/transaction job as nonblocking. Permission and financial-atomicity regression failures can therefore leave the overall workflow successful. A separately configured required job check could still block merging; branch-protection settings were not inspected.
status_and_next_action: **Open; code-only.** After establishing a reliable isolated baseline, remove `continue-on-error` and require the security/transaction check in branch protection.

finding: The locked dependency graph has published security advisories. Bun returned 39 advisory records across 12 package names, representing 33 unique advisory URLs: 24 high, 11 moderate and 4 low records. finding: Analytics collection policy is implicit. The root initializes GA whenever an ID exists, including admin/private routes, without a consent predicate. Third-party automatic history/error enrichment is outside the application fields fixed in AUD-01. By contrast, the separate public-metrics adapter explicitly requires consent.
status_and_next_action: **Open; code-only; product/privacy decision.** Decide collector scope, consent and admin/private-page policy. Validate GA enhanced-measurement/history settings and error-SDK URL enrichment with network capture. This report does not assert a legal violation or that automatic collection is currently enabled.

finding: PayPal OAuth/order/capture/verification and Turnstile fetches have no application deadline or caller abort signal. A stalled provider can hold a donation/submission request until a runtime/network timeout. COD already implements a bounded transport, so resilience differs by provider.
status_and_next_action: **Open; code-only.** Add bounded transport with injected clocks/abort signals and tests for stalls, preserving existing checkout idempotency and uncertain-outcome recovery. Choose a deadline that fits the deployment budget; do not blindly retry capture/creation.

finding: Production-facing URLs can silently use development defaults. An absent `APP_URL` produces localhost links in callbacks, email and receipt assets; PayPal defaults to the sandbox API. Readiness currently checks other capabilities rather than these values.
status_and_next_action: **Open; code-only; deployment configuration decision.** Confirm the canonical production origin and PayPal mode, then validate these explicitly for enabled features. Do not hardcode an inferred domain or switch payment environments during cleanup.
